title: Planes Stop Flying All Over the U.S.
summary:
On Friday, planes all over the United States stopped flying. The Federal Aviation Administration, or FAA, keeps air travel safe. It told all planes to stay on the ground, saying this was needed for "extraordinary circumstances" and "reasons of safety." Runways were empty, and hundreds of flights could not take off.

A ground stop means planes must stay on the ground. Planes already in the sky still landed safely. A stop for the whole country almost never happens. It was only the third one in many years; the last one was in January 2023, when a system for pilots stopped working.

Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said the problem did not look like an attack. He said it looked like a phone and computer problem, and people did not need to be afraid.

No one knows yet what went wrong. Planes are guided by 22 centers, linked by old phone lines. Some people think the link broke. Others blame old tools, like floppy disks and paper strips. Everyone was safe, but many travelers had to wait a long time.
why_it_matters: If you ever fly with your family, a ground stop could delay your trip, so it helps to know why planes sometimes have to wait.
